correctness.rationale: The centered Gaussian KL identity fixes both the orientation and trace scale. The coordinate derivative has cubic numerator P whose derivative is strictly positive for all positive coordinates by Cauchy–Schwarz and a negative-discriminant argument, forcing endpoint spectra. Substitution yields the exact discrete maximum, a unique continuous critical fraction and the large-contrast limit. The proof explicitly handles n=2, the normalization and nonflat equality cases. The embedded deterministic checker passed 385 exact rational identities, 3,048 vertex enumerations, 18,900 interior samples, 14,000 derivative tests, 180 critical-point checks, and 16 large-contrast tests; it is corroboration rather than the universal proof.

value.rationale: A trace-preserving isotropic complement covariance is a natural and explicitly used approximation in matrix-free Lanczos uncertainty models. Determining the exact worst-case forward-KL cost with fixed condition-number budget and dimension replaces a loose quadratic bound by a sharp finite-dimensional formula, locates the equality spectra and isolates the large-contrast coefficient with dimension parity. This gives a meaningful conditioning diagnostic and benchmark; it is not merely an unmotivated scalar evaluation.
